text: A pointwise logistic Factorization Machine with linear terms and k=16 pairwise embeddings over user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, and duration_bucket reproduced the official baseline without a measurable primary-score change: 0.6010 versus 0.6016, a difference of 0.0006 within seed noise.

Among the tested recency-weighted pointwise GBDT, within-user LambdaRank, and empirical-Bayes history variants, the selected LambdaRank GBDT plus FM-incumbent blend did not measurably improve ranking: its 0.6019 primary differed from the official baseline by 0.0003 and from the reproduced FM by 0.0009.

The tested nonlinear NFM interactions, explicit DCN cross layers, latent user-video SVD, and their selected blends did not establish a measurable improvement over the official baseline, reproduced FM, or preceding incumbent: the selected result scored 0.6029 and every corresponding gain was below 0.002.

Iteration 4's validation-selected causal DIN positive-history attention result scored 0.6042, measurably above the 0.6016 official baseline and 0.6010 reproduced FM, but only 0.0013 above the preceding 0.6029 incumbent; without individual xDeepFM and MMoE scores, the evidence does not establish DIN's superiority over those alternatives.

With identical 7-day-half-life recency weighting, AutoInt, FiBiNET, PNN, and BST were not measurably distinguishable: standalone primary ranged from 0.602530 to 0.604228. BST was the numerical winner and produced an incumbent blend near 0.604676, but the margins do not establish superiority of sequence self-attention.

Iteration 6 numerically favored the user-balanced wide-and-deep model with an incumbent blend, but its final primary of 0.6047 matched the preceding result within noise; because individual candidate ranking scores were not reported, the experiment establishes neither a benefit from user balancing nor measurable superiority over the other

In iteration 7's standalone comparison with a 5-day recency half-life, DCNv2 at 0.603508 and PLE at 0.602707 were not measurably different; DCNv2 was measurably above FFM at 0.600260 and within-user BPR-FM at 0.598346, providing no evidence that pairwise BPR supervision is more robust than the strongest tested pointwise alternatives.

Iterations 8-11 retained the trusted incumbent rather than any new candidate.
